title: I shipped a Godot 4 game with an AI coding agent writing the code: pixel art stored as text, music made by a script, and a game that records its own trailer
author: voxtrics_games
selftext:
Long story short - I'm a basic frontend dev, who doesn't have any experience with game dev, but I'm like to playing diff games on mobile, pc, etc. And I always was dreamed about making my own game, but because I don't know about how its working and I didn't have enough time to look into it it always was just a dream. 

And this year I had an idea about resale sim. Imagine you burned out at work and quit you job, soon you need to pay a rent but you don't have enough money so you decided to use some online platform for selling your own staff. This is what "Still available?" about. 

**Prototype** So what I did. I made first prototype myself using HTML + CSS + TS. I send link for it to my friends and asked if it interesting or not. Than using Claude I start to discuss with him what is better to use if I want to release this game everywhere (Play market, AppStore, Steam). Together we decided that Godot is really good. And now I can say that for my game it was a good idea, it has everything what I need. Claude ported my prototype step by step into Godot 4. First game was just blank without pixel art. When we confirmed that everything ported like I wanted we started to add pixel art. 

  
**Pixel art as text.** Every item sprite is a 16×16 grid stored as rows of letters in a JSON file, where each letter is a colour from a shared palette. It sounds odd, but it means the agent can read, draw and fix sprites like any other code, and the whole game keeps one palette. A PNG with the same name replaces the text version, so hand-drawn art can still go in later. All screens are built from code too. We tried a pixel font for the text, but it read badly on phones, so the pixel look moved into buttons and boxes instead. Most hard icon was a general coat. We made mayb 5 or 6 iteration.  

**Sound as code.** There are no audio files made by hand or by an audio model. A Godot script synthesizes every sound from square and triangle waves and noise, plus rain on the window and four slow lo-fi tunes. Changing a sound means changing its recipe and running the script again. With making rain sound we had a lot of interaction, first it sounded more like noise than like rain, so you need to review what Claude did. 

**Balance by bot**. Everytime when we change some logic or trying to fix balance bot helped to check it. We have percentage of how successful game was in prev version and how now. We can easily run 300.

**Translations.** Claude helped me also to translate whole game on 11 languages. Where I had a problems here - first he didn't translate NPC name for different locales, and items name too and it looked strange, so I also had to tell him that he should translate not only "general" words in game but made game specific to each area. 

**Where you still need a human.** Of course any feature you still need to test on real device (like with game which was written by hands). Sometimes AI doesn't understand that he did not what you wanted (like with sounds or art in game). 

Now game is available only on Google play. I hope that AppStore and Steam is on its way and soon will be released too. 

Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.voxtrics.available](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.voxtrics.available)
